meta.title: Think Like an Entrepreneur, Act Like a CEO
meta.author: Beverly E. Jones

parts.title: Summary of Praise for Bev Jones' Book

sentences: **Praise Highlights**: The book, *"Think Like an Entrepreneur, Act Like a CEO,"* by **Beverly E. Jones** is lauded for its **practical career guidance** and **motivating tone**.
Filled with **50 tips**, it offers strategies to thrive and advance in any work environment.
Bev's philosophy revolves around **resilience, adaptability,** and thinking like an entrepreneur while acting as an effective **leader**.
Ideal for those navigating **career shifts** or dealing with tricky workplace challenges.
Her **hands-on advice** encourages building skills for ongoing **success**.

parts.title: Plan and Adapt for Success at New Job

sentences: When starting a new job, you need a **good plan** and should consider what your **boss wants**, work on **meeting people**, and focus on **listening**.
Set yourself **short-term goals**, focus on specifics like **meeting deadlines**, and **adjust your attitude** to deal with challenges.
Use this **intense initial period** to learn everything you can, manage your time, and build your **presence** in the new role.
This planning is essential to understanding your **mission** and knowing how to better **serve customers** and consider learning **business basics** to evaluate operations.
Embrace **failure** as a part of learning, manage stress, and use strategies like **building your brand** to craft a professional image aligned with your goals.
Start planning for a smooth transition and quick adaptation to your new role and responsibilities by addressing these aspects.
**Dress up** a bit in an ensemble to make a **strong start**.
If you're hoping for a **promotion**, dress like you've **climbed the ladder**.
When you **interview** for a **new position**, dress conservatively to **fit in** while being slightly **over-dressed** to show you **care**.
My mother, **Lorna**, says dressing well can challenge **stereotypes** about age.
In work settings, **personal image** suggests how you **value** your work and how you expect to be treated.

parts.title: Overcoming the Fear of Being a Suck-Up

sentences: Often, **self-aware** individuals fear looking like a **suck-up** and avoid complimenting others.
However, it is important to recognize when offering praise is authentic and beneficial.
For instance, supporting a **positive environment** or being genuine when you express respect or gratitude can foster better **relationships** and contribute to team **cohesion**.
By letting go of the fear of being perceived as a brown-noser, you can more freely offer **sincere admiration** and **support**, thus enhancing the work atmosphere and promoting **harmony**.
**Networking** is about **systematic method** to connect with potential colleagues and friends who can offer **career opportunities** and **advise**.
With names of **contacts**, use coffee chats to explore trends and grow professional ties.
Leverage **social media**, especially **LinkedIn** and **Twitter**, to reach recruiters and peers.
**Learning new skills** through **classes** or **online courses** can enhance creativity and **commitment** to excellence.
By **volunteering**, you gain **new experience** and build skills beyond your current job.
Finding a **supportive buddy** can ease the process of **career change** through **idea-sharing** and **motivation**.
Saying **"I'm sorry"** too often can undermine one's confidence, as seen in Tina's case, who developed a habit of apologizing unnecessarily.
Her colleagues found it **annoying**, and she worked to overcome it.
To assess your own habits, consider maintaining a **log for a few weeks** documenting every apology, the reason, and its impact.
This exercise can help increase self-awareness and determine if speech patterns need adjustment.
**Your approach to punctuality** matters in your career.
Generally, it's crucial to **be on time** in professional settings to align with American business etiquette.
However, punctuality can be a cultural matter, as expectations vary widely.
Being late could be seen as disrespectful, while **fanatic over-attention** to timing could be considered **obnoxious**.
To fit in, observe your environment's norms and adjust accordingly.
Punctuality impacts how others view you and can affect your brand and relationships at work.
Consider these strategies to better manage your time: **Know the rules** within your organization, **bank goodwill** by often being on time, and understand the **message** your **behaviors send**.
Don't stress if you're kept waiting; understand that latecomers likely have issues unrelated to you.
Respect your team by ensuring leadership is punctual, and if there's a conflict in views, **talk and establish standards** for efficiency and mutual respect.
Adapting these strategies can help manage punctuality more effectively and improve team dynamics.

parts.title: Navigating Organizational Change: Resilience and Strategy

sentences: In navigating organizational change, staying resilient and focused is crucial.
**Andrea Wilkinson**, a seasoned professional in the biopharmaceutical industry, has thrived amid extensive restructuring.
Her strategy involves recognizing that changes are not personal but part of a broader organizational challenge—much like a storm affecting everyone, where bitterness could worsen one's situation.
It's important to focus on the big picture and how you fit into the future rather than dwelling on the past.
Understanding your field is vital for staying adaptable in a shifting environment.
**Andrea's success** lies in her proactive approach, always assessing industry trends and leveraging her insights to make informed decisions.

Instead of fixating on unwanted changes, she strives to understand the implications, strategize actively, and seize new opportunities that arise from such transitions, ensuring stable career progression amid uncertainties.
**Take Care of Yourself:** It's important to stay **energetic** during times of change.
Instead of exhausting yourself, maintain a regular **fitness routine** and get enough **sleep** to sustain energy.
Andrea knows this well and ensures she is in **great shape** to handle transitions at work.
**Manage Finances Wisely:** Andrea doesn't rely solely on her job; she avoids financial **desperation** by managing her investments prudently.
In uncertain times, having a "rainy day fund" or alternative income sources can offer **stability** and even **energize** your main job.
A **side gig** can spark **creativity** and renew enthusiasm.
